# Internal Petstore service.
#
# All endpoints require a bearer token except the health check. Rate limits
# apply to the search endpoints, so keep an eye on the X-RateLimit headers when
# running the whole folder.
# @auth basic {{user}} hunter2
@baseUrl = https://petstore.example.com
@user = alice

// Postman test script for "Petstore API", translated as far as it goes.

// **Nothing runs this file.** It is a plain ES module (docs/FORMAT.md §2.4),
// because something in it has no Otis equivalent:
//
//   line 1, pm.expect — that is chai; Otis' expect has toBe, toEqual and a handful more, with no chained `.to.have` (docs/FORMAT.md §9.9).
//
// The rest was translated. Finish the port and rename the file to _post.js to make
// Otis run it, or move what you need into a {% %} block in the request.
//
// A script gets a JavaScript realm and nothing else: no fetch, no require, no
// filesystem, no timers (docs/FORMAT.md §9.3).

test("fast", () => pm.expect(response.timings.total).to.be.below(500));

// Postman pre-request script for "Pets", translated as far as it goes.
//
// **Nothing runs this file.** It is a plain ES module (docs/FORMAT.md §2.4),
// because something in it has no Otis equivalent:
//
//   line 1, pm. — Otis has no equivalent for this call, or it needs a decision a table cannot make.
//
// The rest was translated. Finish the port and rename the file to _pre.js to make
// Otis run it, or move what you need into a {% %} block in the request.
//
// A script gets a JavaScript realm and nothing else: no fetch, no require, no
// filesystem, no timers (docs/FORMAT.md §9.3).

vars.session.set("requestId", pm.variables.replaceIn("{{$guid}}"));

=== pets/create-pet.post.js ===
// Postman test script for "Create pet", translated.
//
// **This runs.** It is a hook (docs/FORMAT.md §2.4), so Otis executes it
// around the request it belongs to, exactly as Postman did.
//
// What was substituted:
//
//   1 → response.json
//   1 → vars.session.set
//
// A Postman variable set became vars.session.set: in memory, on this machine,
// written to no file, and visible to every request in this folder and below
// (docs/FORMAT.md §4.5). If you meant the value to persist, vars.env.set
// writes the active environment file — and shows up in git.

const pet = response.json();
vars.session.set("petId", pet.id);
console.log("petId", pet.id);

=== search/_pre.js ===
// Postman pre-request script for "Search", translated.
//
// **This runs.** It is a hook (docs/FORMAT.md §2.4), so Otis executes it
// around the request it belongs to, exactly as Postman did.
//
// What was substituted:
//
//   1 → vars.session.set
//
// A Postman variable set became vars.session.set: in memory, on this machine,
// written to no file, and visible to every request in this folder and below
// (docs/FORMAT.md §4.5). If you meant the value to persist, vars.env.set
// writes the active environment file — and shows up in git.

// Postman wrote this into the environment; Otis keeps it in the session.
vars.session.set("searchStartedAt", new Date().toISOString());
=== search/graphql-search.http ===
# @name GraphQL search
POST {{baseUrl}}/graphql
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "query": "query Search($q: String!) {\n  pets(query: $q) {\n    id\n    name\n  }\n}",
  "variables": {
    "q": "rex"
  }
}

Needs attention (9)
  - _folder.http: basic password is a literal value in the collection; move it to an environment variable
  - _postman-post.js: test script for "Petstore API" needs pm.expect; imported as a module, so nothing runs it until you port it to _post.js
  - pets/_postman-pre.js: pre-request script for "Pets" needs pm.; imported as a module, so nothing runs it until you port it to _pre.js
  - pets/get-pet.postman-post.js: test script for "Get pet" needs pm.expect; imported as a module, so nothing runs it until you port it to get-pet.post.js
  - pets/upload-photo.http: form file "photo" points at /Users/alice/Pictures/rex.jpg, a path on the exporting machine; copy the file into the collection and fix the path
  - infra-aws/s3-object-literal-keys.http: AWS secret key was a literal in the export; replaced with {{awsSecretKey}}. Set it as a keychain secret, or switch to '@auth aws profile=<name>' to use your local AWS credentials
  - infra-aws/s3-object-literal-keys.http: AWS session token was a literal in the export; replaced with {{awsSessionToken}}
  - env/petstore-dev.json: secret variables written as keychain references; their values were NOT imported and must be stored in the keychain: token, apiKey
  - pets/_postman-pre.js: Postman dynamic variable {{$guid}} has no Otis equivalent and will be reported as unresolved

Notes (9)
